lsh_the_masts_are_gone.accept_text:
Forty years I have priced freight on this coast and every single price had the Southsea in it. A sixth for the cove, we called it. Nobody wrote it down, it was just in the number.

I have spent this morning repricing everything and I do not mind telling you it has made me feel strange. Go and stand on the Upper Yard, just west of this desk, and look north and come back.

lsh_the_prize_court.turn_in_text:
[She reads for a long time.]

Names. Two of them are dead, one of them left with the Gadgetzan crowd, and one of them is still trading out of the Upper Yard.

I am not going to tell you which. I am going to walk over there this afternoon and have a conversation, and whatever else happens, they are going to know that I know.

lsh_recognising_my_own_stock.accept_text:
I buy what came off something and I sell it onto something else and I have never once pretended otherwise.

What I will not do is buy my own stock back. Twice this season somebody has put a crate on my counter that I SOLD, out of this shop, six weeks before.

Get me the tags off them. Hesper inks every crate that leaves this port and they have been re-inking over the top, and badly.

The ones doing the re-inking are the Southsea riggers. The prize tags are on them.

lsh_my_own_powder.accept_text:
I build things that mostly work and I am honest about the mostly, so I am going to be honest about this: I sold them the powder.

Not knowingly. A freight agent I will not name, a standing order, four years of it, and I never once asked where it went because the money was good and I had a workshop to replace.

Go and get me a keg back. I want to see my own cooperage mark with a scrape through it.

The Southsea powdermonkeys keep the kegs. You will not get one without a fight.

lsh_the_boarding_nets.accept_text:
A fishing net is weighted evenly. A boarding net is weighted at the HEM so it drops flat over a deck and nobody under it can stand up.

I have mended both for thirty years and I can tell them apart in the dark. Bring me what they are using and I will tell the harbourmaster exactly what her crews are walking into.

The Southsea netcasters carry them.

lsh_the_bosun.accept_text:
Here is what I have worked out about that cove and it is the only useful thing anybody has said about it in twenty years.

They are hulls lashed together. One plank between each. There is no going round, for you OR for them - which means you can take it apart one deck at a time and they cannot flank you, and it also means every single plank has somebody standing on it.

The first one is Grell Tarpot. You will hear him before you see him.

His swabbies will come at you on the plank before he does.

lsh_the_sailmaker.accept_text:
There is a sailmaker on that fleet. I have thought about that more than is healthy.

Nobody on those hulls has unfurled a sail in twenty years. So either she has had nothing to do for two decades, or she has been making something else - and I have seen the nets, so I know which.

She will be on the careenage. That is the hull laid over to have its bottom scraped, and they never righted it, and I think about that one too.

Hulk rats have the run of that hull. Clear them on your way to her.
